# CLEARS - Model Evaluation Report
**Owner:** Person 2 - ML & Explainability Lead | **Generated by:** `src/make_model_report.py` from `data/models/metrics.json`
**Data:** `features_final.csv` (see `docs/data_quality_report.md`) | **Library versions:** XGBoost 3.2.0, scikit-learn 1.8.0, pandas 2.2.3

> **Headline.** On a time-ordered, out-of-sample test set the disruption model reaches **F1 = 0.365** for the disruption class
> (precision 0.323, recall 0.420) and **ROC-AUC = 0.662**. The project target of F1 >= 0.70 is
> **NOT met**. A date-grouped cross-validation, which is easier than a time-ordered test, reaches only
> F1 = 0.399 and ROC-AUC = 0.713, so the gap to 0.70 is not caused by the
> split. The data were regenerated from the raw NOAA and BTS files (weather in correct local time, each flight once); they still cover only four months a year and two airports.

## 1. Model architecture
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Disruption model | `XGBClassifier`, binary, `scale_pos_weight` = 4.80 (negatives / positives in training), histogram trees |
| Selected hyper-parameters | max_depth 5, learning_rate 0.1, 64 trees (early stopping, 30 rounds, validation PR-AUC), subsample 0.8, colsample 0.8, min_child_weight 5 |
| Search | guide grid (depth 3/5/7 x learning rate 0.05/0.1), n_estimators by early stopping; chosen on the **validation** slice by PR-AUC. All six configurations scored within 0.002 PR-AUC of each other |
| Probability calibration | isotonic regression fitted on the validation slice, so `probability` is a real probability (the raw `scale_pos_weight` output is inflated: Brier 0.2238 raw vs 0.1398 calibrated vs 0.1501 for a constant) |
| Decision threshold | 0.224 on the calibrated probability, the F1-optimal value on the validation slice |
| Inputs (20) | `wind_speed_knots`, `visibility_km`, `temperature_c`, `humidity_pct`, `precip_mm_hr`, `wind_category_enc`, `visibility_risk`, `rain_severity_enc`, `temp_stress`, `storm_flag`, `hour_of_day`, `day_of_week`, `month`, `is_peak_hour`, `is_weekend`, `delay_last_1h`, `delay_last_3h`, `delay_last_24h`, `congestion_level`, `runway_count` |
| Excluded | every label-derived column (`dep_delay`, `arr_delay`, `delay_minutes`, `cancelled`, `*_delay`), identifiers and constants - see `docs/feature_dictionary.md` Section 9 |
| Severity model | `XGBClassifier(objective='multi:softprob', num_class=4)`, balanced sample weights, depth 3, learning rate 0.1, 54 trees |
| Scenario (what-if) model | XGBoost on weather + time + airport only (no delay history), monotone constraints, depth 3, learning rate 0.03, 2385 trees, isotonic-calibrated |
| Saved files | `data/models/disruption_model.pkl`, `severity_model.pkl`, `scenario_model.pkl` (dicts holding the model, calibrator, threshold, feature list and training medians; load with the same library versions) |

## 2. Training data
| Slice | Dates | Rows | Disruption rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Train | 2019-01-01 to 2021-07-31 | 240,496 | 17.2% |
| Validation (early stopping, calibration, threshold) | 2021-10-01 to 2022-01-31 | 46,979 | 20.1% |
| **Test (used once)** | 2022-04-01 to 2022-10-31 | 71,119 | 18.4% |

Airports ORD and MEM, only January/April/July/October of each year (492 days). Split on whole dates, strictly time-ordered; the test set
contains **no winter month** (April, July and October 2022 only). Class ratio about 4.8 : 1.

## 4. Comparison with baselines
| Model | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | F1 (disruption) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flag every flight | 0.500 | 0.184 | 0.310 |
| Delay-history signal alone (`delay_last_3h` as a score) | 0.636 | 0.288 | - |
| Logistic regression (same 20 inputs, same protocol) | 0.652 | 0.316 | 0.351 |
| **XGBoost (this model)** | **0.662** | **0.336** | **0.365** |

XGBoost improves on logistic regression by 0.014 F1 (4.0% relative) and 0.009 ROC-AUC. That is a small
gain, not the "substantial improvement" the project report expects. A weather-only XGBoost scores ROC-AUC 0.590 and
F1 0.332; flagging every flight scores F1 0.310.

**Which inputs matter (retrained on feature groups, same protocol)**

| Feature group | Inputs | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| full | 20 | 0.662 | 0.336 | 0.365 |
| weather only | 10 | 0.590 | 0.229 | 0.332 |
| time only | 6 | 0.611 | 0.236 | 0.340 |
| no history features | 16 | 0.640 | 0.269 | 0.359 |

Delay history is worth about +0.022 ROC-AUC on top of weather + time; weather alone scores ROC-AUC 0.590, time alone 0.611.

**Is the low score a split artefact?** No.

| Evaluation | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time-ordered test (this report) | 0.662 | 0.336 | 0.365 |
| Train before 2022, test 2022 (whole year) | 0.667 | 0.360 | - |
| Train before 2021, test 2021 | 0.707 | 0.374 | - |
| Date-grouped 5-fold CV (optimistic, not time-ordered) | 0.713 | 0.401 | 0.399 |

## 5. Top 10 SHAP features (mean |SHAP| on the test set, log-odds of the raw model)
SHAP values are exact TreeSHAP from XGBoost (`pred_contribs`), identical to `shap.TreeExplainer`; they sum to the model output (checked in `model_verification.md`). Plot: `assets/shap_summary.png`.

| # | Feature | Mean abs SHAP | Share | What it measures | Does it make sense? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `delay_last_3h` | 0.2782 | 24.5% | Share of flights disrupted in the 3-hour window ending two hours before this flight | Delays cascade: a disrupted airport tends to stay disrupted. The strongest and most intuitive signal. |
| 2 | `hour_of_day` | 0.1544 | 13.6% | Scheduled departure hour | Delays accumulate through the day, so late hours are riskier (about 8.5% at 05:00, 21-25% between 15:00 and 22:00). |
| 3 | `delay_last_1h` | 0.1340 | 11.8% | Disruption share in the single hour ending two hours before | Same cascade effect, shorter memory. |
| 4 | `delay_last_24h` | 0.1315 | 11.6% | Disruption share over the previous 24 hours | Captures a bad day (weather system, ground stop) rather than a bad hour. |
| 5 | `congestion_level` | 0.1104 | 9.7% | Scheduled departures in the two previous hours | A busier airport has less slack; plausible, and it also proxies the time of day. |
| 6 | `temperature_c` | 0.0927 | 8.2% | Air temperature | Acts mostly as a season proxy (hot July afternoons with thunderstorms and high traffic) rather than a direct cause. |
| 7 | `humidity_pct` | 0.0775 | 6.8% | Relative humidity | Also season/convective-weather proxy; not a direct operational driver. |
| 8 | `visibility_km` | 0.0370 | 3.3% | Horizontal visibility | Low visibility forces instrument procedures and spacing; sensible, but a small effect once delay history is known. |
| 9 | `precip_mm_hr` | 0.0328 | 2.9% | Precipitation intensity | Rain slows operations; very small effect in this data. |
| 10 | `day_of_week` | 0.0220 | 1.9% | Day of week | Weekly traffic pattern (Sunday highest, Tuesday lowest). |

**The weather flags the project report names as leading predictors contribute almost nothing:** `visibility_risk` 0.06%, `storm_flag` 0.02%,
`wind_category_enc` 0.05% of total importance; only `delay_last_3h` (24.5%) is a leading predictor. The flags are rare (storm flag 0.48% of flights) and the model
reads the same information from the raw weather columns instead (`visibility_km`, `precip_mm_hr`, `wind_speed_knots` together 7.7% of total importance). Weather clearly matters in the raw data:
flights with visibility < 3 km are disrupted 36.5% of the time vs 17.5% otherwise, but those flights are few and delay history explains most of the rest.

## 6. Delay severity model
Classes: none (not disrupted), minor (15-45 min), moderate (45-120 min), severe (> 120 min). Balanced class weights.

| Class | Test flights | Precision | Recall | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 58,051 | 0.872 | 0.643 | 0.740 |
| minor | 6,554 | 0.109 | 0.224 | 0.147 |
| moderate | 4,734 | 0.115 | 0.218 | 0.150 |
| severe | 1,780 | 0.080 | 0.267 | 0.123 |

Accuracy 0.567, **macro-F1 0.290** (always predicting "none" would score accuracy 0.816 but macro-F1 about 0.2). Confusion matrix (rows = truth, columns = prediction):

| | none | minor | moderate | severe |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| true none | 37,319 | 10,622 | 6,410 | 3,700 |
| true minor | 3,038 | 1,466 | 1,193 | 857 |
| true moderate | 1,838 | 950 | 1,032 | 914 |
| true severe | 587 | 353 | 364 | 476 |

The severity classes are only weakly separable from the available inputs (F1 0.123-0.150 for the three delay classes). Use the severity output as a coarse indication and show the class probabilities, not the label alone.

## 7. Probability bands and the dashboard
With the calibrated probability, KPI 4 bands (Low < 0.3, Medium 0.3-0.65, High > 0.65) split the test flights as:

| Band | Share of flights | Observed disruption rate |
|---|---|---|
| Low | 91.5% | 15.9% |
| Medium | 6.8% | - |
| High | 1.7% | 65.4% |

The probabilities are well calibrated at the top (High-band flights are disrupted 65% of the time), but with an 18% base rate 92% of flights are "Low" and only 1.7% are "High", so the gauge will
rarely leave green. The team should choose bands with this in mind (for example by relative risk: base rate x 1.5, x 2).

## 8. Scenario simulator
`scenario_risk(base, overrides)` re-scores a flight with changed weather. By default it uses the **full model**, so `base_probability` equals the dashboard gauge. Raw weather overrides are
turned into the flags and encodings the model reads (a scenario row cannot contradict itself); the flight's delay-history inputs stay as they are, so this answers "what if the weather were different and nothing else changed".
`mode='weather'` uses a second model without delay history (monotone: worse weather never lowers the risk; test ROC-AUC 0.633), i.e. "the risk under these conditions before delays have accumulated".

Mean predicted probability on 5,000 test flights; "historical" is the observed disruption rate of all flights in the data under comparable conditions.

| Scenario | Historical flights in comparable conditions | Full model: probability (change) | Weather-only model: probability (change) |
|---|---|---|---|
| no override | all flights: 18.4% (test) | 18.7% | 19.5% |
| low visibility (0.5 km) (`visibility_km=0.5`) | visibility < 1 km: n = 1,216, 40.1% disrupted | 25.4% (+7 pts) | 32.3% (+13 pts) |
| heavy rain (10 mm/h) (`precip_mm_hr=10.0`) | rain >= 7.5 mm/h: n = 540, 45.9% disrupted | 35.0% (+16 pts) | 55.0% (+35 pts) |
| strong wind (28 kn) (`wind_speed_knots=28.0`) | wind >= 25 kn: n = 1,013, 27.1% disrupted | 22.5% (+4 pts) | 36.8% (+17 pts) |
| all three together (`visibility_km=0.5, precip_mm_hr=10.0, wind_speed_knots=28.0`) | visibility < 1 km and rain >= 2.5 mm/h: n = 70, 34.3% disrupted | 52.1% (+33 pts) | 81.0% (+61 pts) |
| clear day (16 km, dry, 5 kn) (`visibility_km=16.0, precip_mm_hr=0.0, wind_speed_knots=5.0`) | visibility >= 10 km, dry, wind < 10 kn: n = 212,798, 15.9% disrupted | 17.9% (-1 pts) | 18.3% (-1 pts) |

Single conditions land in the right range (heavy rain: 46% observed; the models say about 35% / 55%).
**The combined "all three" scenario goes beyond the data**: only 70 historical flights had visibility < 1 km together with rain >= 2.5 mm/h (34% disrupted), yet the models extrapolate far higher.
Treat combined extremes as an upper bound, not a forecast. Wind above the training maximum (35 kn) is treated like ~35 kn.

*History:* on the earlier data version, whose weather was 5-6 hours out of sync with departure times, the full model barely reacted to weather overrides (about +4 points for the same severe override); the weather-only model was added to fix that.
The reaction came back once the weather was aligned, which is why the full model is now the default and the weather-only model is optional.

## 9. Resilience index methodology
Inputs per airport (from `data/processed/airport_resilience_inputs.csv`): disruption rate, average delay of disrupted flights ("recovery time"), weather sensitivity = correlation(`storm_flag`, `disruption`), congestion sensitivity = correlation(`congestion_level`, `disruption`).
Formula: min-max normalise each across airports; vulnerability = 0.35 x disruption rate + 0.30 x recovery time + 0.20 x weather sensitivity + 0.15 x congestion sensitivity; index = 100 - 100 x vulnerability; tiers <= 40 Vulnerable, 40-70 Moderate, > 70 Resilient.
Weights are a design choice: frequency (0.35) and severity of delays (0.30) are what operations experience most directly; the two correlation terms (0.20 / 0.15) describe sensitivity rather than outcomes and are weaker, noisier measures. The literature does not fix the weights.

| Airport | Disruption rate | Avg delay of disrupted flights (min) | Weather sens. | Congestion sens. | Resilience index | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MEM | 0.1542 | 70.3 | 0.0521 | 0.0503 | **50.0** | Moderate |
| ORD | 0.1804 | 68.2 | 0.0429 | 0.0800 | **50.0** | Moderate |

**Limitation that matters:** with two airports min-max scaling maps every dimension to exactly 0 or 1, so the scores only say which airport is higher on each dimension, not by how much. This makes the index unstable:
on the earlier data version (weather misaligned, duplicated flights) it was ORD 30, MEM 70; on the corrected data it is ORD 50, MEM 50.
The change comes from one reversed ordering (weather sensitivity: MEM 0.0521 vs ORD 0.0429 after the correction), not from any real change in the airports.
In the test months MEM's disruption rate (20.7%) is higher than ORD's (18.2%), the opposite of the full-period ranking. Do not present the index as more than a two-airport ranking; it needs >= 4 airports or fixed reference ranges.

## 11. Known limitations
1. **Weather alignment was fixed in this version** (NOAA UTC times converted to local time; the earlier data was 5-6 hours out of sync - data quality report, Check 8). What remains: one weather station per airport, observations up to an hour old at departure time, and precipitation only from the first ISD precipitation group.
2. **Modest predictive power.** F1 0.365 / ROC-AUC 0.662; even the optimistic date-grouped CV only reaches F1 0.399. The inputs (weather, time, short delay history) do not determine disruption well; schedule, airline and route data would be needed.
3. **Small, unrepresentative coverage:** four months per year, two airports, no winter month in the test set, 2020 is an outlier year. 15,875 cancelled flights (4.2% of scheduled departures) have no departure delay and were removed, so disruption is understated.
4. **Regime shift:** thresholds tuned on the October-January validation slice do not transfer to October 2022 (F1 0.116 that month).
5. **Extreme and combined weather scenarios extrapolate** beyond the data (section 8).
6. **No real-time feed:** inputs are historical; delay-history features need a live feed in production.
7. **Severity model is weak** (macro-F1 0.290).
8. **Statements in the project report that this evidence does not support** (for Person 4 to correct): the abstract's "F1 score exceeding 0.70" and "substantial improvement over logistic regression"; Chapter 5's claim that SHAP confirmed `visibility_risk`, `storm_flag` and `wind_category` as leading predictors (they contribute under 0.1% each); the recommendation bands (0.50/0.80) which do not match the KPI bands used here.
